newsitem.title: UK: UK utilities slide on windfall tax worries.
newsitem.headline: UK utilities slide on windfall tax worries.

text.p: Shares in British utility and water companies dropped on Monday after Gordon Brown, shadow finance minister for the opposition Labour Party, said a Labour government would impose a windfall tax on privatised utilities.
Among leading water companies, Anglian Water was down 12p at 538p, United Utilities was down 12p at 571p and Yorkshire Water dropped 11p to 630p.
Among power companies, PowerGen was down eight pence at 487-1/2p and National Power shed four pence to 393p.
Brown said the windfall tax would aim to create job opportunities and reduce social security bills.

Traders said investors were also unsettled by a report in the weekend's Financial Times that cited an aide to Brown saying the tax could be extended beyond water and electricity to all privatised utilities, including gas and telecommunications.
"The problem is that the windfall tax could be on a broader base of the utilities sector than was expected," said David Campbell, analyst at Greig Middleton.

The report, citing the aide, said estimates that between three and five billion stg could be raised by the windfall tax were conservative. It said another senior Labour party source had estimated that 10 billion stg could be raised.
"It's not surprising the shares are weak if people think taxes could be three times what they expected," Campbell said.
